channel.title: WP Digests — security
channel.description: Notable WordPress ecosystem changes in the security track.

item.title: WordPress 7.0.2 Release
item.description:
WordPress 7.0.2 is a security release that patches one critical and one high-severity vulnerability. The critical issue combines a REST API batch-route confusion bug with SQL injection to achieve Remote Code Execution, and the high-severity issue is a separately reported, facilitated SQL injection. Because of the severity, WordPress.org enabled forced auto-updates for sites running affected versions rather than waiting for site owners to update manually.
Digest entry: issues/security/wp-news-security-21167.md · Source: WordPress News

item.title: wp2shell Aftermath: The First Critical Unauthenticated WordPress Core RCE in Nearly a Decade
item.description:
WordPress Core shipped emergency patches on July 17, 2026 (versions 6.8.6, 6.9.5, and 7.0.2) for a two-vulnerability chain, dubbed wp2shell, that allows unauthenticated remote code execution against unmodified WordPress installs. The chain combines a SQL injection flaw (CVE-2026-60137) with a second vulnerability (CVE-2026-63030) that together let an attacker execute arbitrary code without any plugin, theme, or authenticated access being involved. WordPress.org rated the pair one critical and one high severity issue and — because of that severity — force-enabled automatic updates across affected versions rather than waiting for sites to update on their own schedule. The chain was discovered and responsibly disclosed by Adam Kues of Assetnote/Searchlight Cyber, and Wordfence is calling it the first critical unauthenticated Core RCE in nearly a decade.
Digest entry: issues/security/wordfence-blog-42501.md · Source: Wordfence Blog

item.title: PSA: WordPress Core Patched Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Vulnerability Chain
item.description:
WordPress core received emergency security updates on July 17, 2026 patching two chainable vulnerabilities: an unauthenticated SQL injection (CVE-2026-60137, CVSS 7.5) via the `author__not_in` parameter affecting core 6.8–7.0.1, and a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-63030, CVSS 9.8) in the REST API batch request route affecting core 6.9–7.0.1. The RCE stems from a route/validation desynchronization in the batch endpoint that lets a validated sub-request be dispatched to an unintended callback, bypassing the `allow_batch` restriction and the target route's input sanitization — when chained with the SQL injection, this can escalate to full unauthenticated remote code execution. WordPress's Security Team pushed automatic background updates to affected sites rather than waiting for manual upgrades, underscoring the severity.
Digest entry: issues/security/wordfence-blog-42493.md · Source: Wordfence Blog

item.title: Aimogen Pro - All-in-One AI Content Writer, Editor, ChatBot & Automation Toolkit <= 2.8.4 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'aiomatic_call_google_ai_function'
item.description:
Aimogen Pro versions ≤ 2.8.4 contain an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in the `aiomatic_call_google_ai_function` callback. The function lacks a capability check, allowing unauthenticated attackers to invoke the `aimogen_wp_god_mode` tool, bypass internal function blacklists, and execute arbitrary PHP code—including creating new administrator accounts. Updating to 2.8.5 enforces proper access controls and closes this execution path.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-53cc91fa-51fd-4d16-b740-a48f8d446b5d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Podlove Podcast Publisher <= 4.5.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via podlove_image_cache_url Parameter
item.description:
Podlove Podcast Publisher versions up to 4.5.1 contain an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in the `podlove_handle_cache_files` function. The flaw stems from missing file type validation on the `podlove_image_cache_url` parameter, allowing attackers to upload arbitrary files to the server. This can lead to remote code execution and requires immediate patching to version 4.5.2 or later.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f81a3429-f378-4295-adbe-ad6f1df59701.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SAML Single Sign On <= 5.4.3 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'SAMLResponse' Parameter Signature Algorithm Confusion
item.description:
The SAML Single Sign On – SSO Login plugin for WordPress has been patched to prevent an unauthenticated authentication bypass. Versions 5.4.3 and earlier incorrectly allowed the `SignatureMethod` algorithm attribute from the incoming `SAMLResponse` to dictate how the IdP’s public key was processed, enabling attackers to force an HMAC-SHA1 validation path and forge valid assertions. Updating to 5.4.4 enforces the locally configured signature algorithm, closing the cryptographic signature confusion vector.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ee95092d-6351-4612-872d-284165bc1201.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Bricksforge <= 3.1.8.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Pro Forms fieldIds Parameter
item.description:
The Bricksforge plugin contains a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in versions up to 3.1.8.6. Improper validation of the `fieldIds` parameter in the Pro Forms registration action allows attackers to inject arbitrary field IDs into a trusted whitelist. This bypasses intended access controls, enabling unauthenticated users to register new administrator accounts on sites that expose a public Bricksforge Pro Forms element configured with the User Registration action.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-d0538778-5ba4-4bec-a89d-ef90a9ba8375.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Paytium: Mollie payment forms & donations <= 5.0.2 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Paytium: Mollie payment forms & donations plugin contained an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in versions up to 5.0.2. The flaw allowed attackers to bypass authentication checks and elevate their user capabilities on affected WordPress installations. The vulnerability was resolved in version 5.0.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-9ef3e6c7-b75a-4afc-b1c7-6e74b0c894a9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Dokan Pro <= 5.0.4 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
Dokan Pro versions up to 5.0.4 contain an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to elevate their user privileges without valid credentials. The issue was resolved in version 5.0.5, which enforces proper capability checks and access controls. Site owners must update to the patched version to prevent unauthorized access.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ad4acbcb-5044-4752-9db0-74bd6f99a963.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SignUp & SignIn <= 1.0.0 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Weak Password Reset Validation via 'reset_activation_code' Leading to Account Takeover
item.description:
The SignUp & SignIn plugin (≤1.0.0) contains an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to reset any user’s password, including administrators, without triggering a legitimate password-reset flow. The flaw stems from the `pravel_change_password()` AJAX handler bypassing nonce verification and capability checks, while relying on a loose equality comparison against the `forgot_email` user meta. Because the meta field defaults to an empty string for users who have never requested a reset, an attacker can supply an empty or omitted `reset_activation_code` to bypass validation entirely. This enables direct account takeover via a single crafted `admin-ajax.php` request.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c0a617fc-da3d-4828-b027-44093dd11769.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Invoice Generator <= 1.0.0 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Weak Password Reset Validation via 'reset_user_id' Parameter
item.description:
The Invoice Generator plugin (≤ 1.0.0) contains a critical unauthenticated account takeover vulnerability in its password reset flow. The `pravel_invoice_change_password()` AJAX handler lacks nonce verification and capability checks, and uses a loose equality comparison that trivially passes when the `reset_activation_code` parameter is omitted. This allows attackers to supply an arbitrary `reset_user_id` and force a password change for any account, including administrators.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cc0fbe84-e455-4e62-9c48-49340d08f81d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: OMGF Pro <= 5.2.6 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via @import URL Reflection
item.description:
The OMGF Pro plugin has been patched to resolve a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability (CVE-2026-57700) that allowed remote code execution. The flaw existed in the `ExternalStylesheets::optimize()` method, which previously fetched external CSS `@import` URLs and wrote their contents directly to the uploads directory without validating file types, checking MIME types, or verifying user capabilities. Updating to version 5.2.7 or later is required to secure affected sites.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5d371a8e-2997-4be3-afd9-60f752a6721c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Invoice Generator <= 1.0.0 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Account Takeover via 'user_id' Parameter
item.description:
The Invoice Generator plugin (≤ 1.0.0) contains a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack any WordPress user account. The flaw stems from a missing capability check on the `pravel_invoice_edit_account()` AJAX handler, which accepts attacker-controlled `user_id` and `user_email` parameters and directly calls `wp_update_user()` without verifying authentication, ownership, or a nonce. This enables unauthenticated users to change any account's email address and subsequently trigger WordPress's native password reset flow to gain full access.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ee045d0d-101a-4ae2-b209-4a4865eec195.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Blocksy Companion Pro <= 2.1.46 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
Blocksy Companion Pro versions up to 2.1.46 contain an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server. The issue was resolved in version 2.1.47, which patches the insecure input handling that previously allowed unauthenticated execution. Site administrators and developers using this companion plugin must update immediately to prevent exploitation.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-0b2051e8-3195-498a-9d76-8645fd8476c1.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProfileGrid - User Profiles, Groups and Communities <= 5.9.9.5 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Email Overwrite
item.description:
The ProfileGrid plugin contained a critical vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the email address of the primary administrator (user ID 1) through registration forms. By exploiting missing validation on the `user_login` parameter and improperly handled error responses, attackers could trigger a password reset and fully compromise the admin account. The issue is resolved in version 5.9.9.6, which enforces strict parameter validation and corrects the error-handling flow.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2d35279d-299e-4ca2-8f84-165284e058c8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: EventON - WordPress Virtual Event Calendar Plugin <= 5.0.11 - Unauthenticated Blind SQL Injection via Search Parameter
item.description:
EventON versions up to 5.0.11 contain an unauthenticated blind SQL injection vulnerability triggered through the WordPress `search` parameter. The flaw stems from insufficient input escaping and missing query preparation, allowing attackers to extract database contents when the "Enable additional search queries" setting is active and at least one event is published. No official patch has been released, so site operators must rely on configuration changes or plugin removal to mitigate the risk.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1b5a0c87-59b0-4da4-8949-0957f8e1b479.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WP-BusinessDirectory <= 4.0.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal via '_filename' Parameter
item.description:
WP-BusinessDirectory versions up to 4.0.1 contain an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability. The flaw stems from insufficient path validation in the `remove()` method of the `JBusinessDirectoryControllerUpload` class, allowing attackers to supply path traversal sequences via the `_filename` parameter. The vendor patch restricts path resolution to prevent deletion of files outside the intended directory.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-d7d68f43-2a57-4352-8aae-0657b386ac7c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SMS Alert <= 3.9.5 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Arbitrary Password Reset
item.description:
The SMS Alert plugin (≤3.9.5) contained an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allowed attackers to reset arbitrary user passwords, including administrators. The flaw occurred because the plugin updated user details without properly validating the requesting user's identity. Patched in 3.9.6, the fix enforces strict identity verification before processing password reset requests.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c31906da-f2fd-40ac-86e0-3f1ed0409d0c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Private Content <= 9.9.2 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Private Content plugin (versions ≤ 9.9.2) contains a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to elevate their capabilities to administrator level without valid credentials. This flaw bypasses WordPress's standard authentication and capability checks, granting full control over the site. The plugin author has not released a patch, so immediate mitigation is required.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-50bdca4a-23c0-46aa-8c08-5987a2e28604.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Divi Form Builder <= 5.1.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload Leading to Remote Code Execution via 'acceptFileTypes' Parameter
item.description:
Divi Form Builder versions up to 5.1.8 contain an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability that enables remote code execution. The `do_image_upload()` function directly interpolates the `acceptFileTypes` POST parameter into a regular expression for file extension validation, allowing attackers to bypass extension checks and upload executable PHP variants such as `.phtml`, `.phar`, `.php5`, or `.php7`. The vulnerability was fully remediated in version 5.1.9 by replacing the dynamic regex interpolation with a strict extension allowlist and enforcing server-side MIME validation before writing files to disk.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-9692deb2-2526-4983-8a13-93a382e230c8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Blocksy Companion <= 2.1.46 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'blc-review-images[]' Parameter
item.description:
Blocksy Companion plugin versions ≤ 2.1.46 contained an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in the `save_attachments` function. A custom `wp_check_filetype_and_ext` filter used substring matching to approve font files, allowing double-extension payloads like `shell.woff2.php` to bypass MIME validation and execute as PHP. Patched in 2.1.47, the fix enforces strict extension validation to prevent remote code execution via uploaded files.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2df449b4-3f3b-4afc-b391-8d8d11710c07.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Printcart Web to Print Product Designer for WooCommerce <= 2.5.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
Printcart Web to Print Product Designer for WooCommerce versions ≤2.5.2 contain a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability (CVE-2026-9725). The flaw stems from insufficient path validation in the `store_design_data()` function, which accepts a user-supplied `nbd_item_key` parameter and passes it directly to `Nbdesigner_IO::delete_folder()` and `rename()` without blocking path traversal sequences. Attackers can bypass the AJAX nonce requirement by fetching it through the `nbd_check_use_logged_in` endpoint, enabling them to delete arbitrary server files and potentially achieve remote code execution. Site owners must update to version 2.5.3 or later immediately.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5bb962bd-9b23-4820-885e-d8095250c3c7.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WPFunnels <= 3.12.7 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via 'postData' Parameter
item.description:
WPFunnels contained a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability triggered via the `postData` parameter. Attackers could inject arbitrary PHP code into a `.log` file through an unsanitized write, which was then executed via `include_once` in the `wpfnl_show_log` function. The plugin has been patched to sanitize input and prevent arbitrary file inclusion, eliminating the execution path.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5d84d749-0ab5-49dd-8e4f-45681f197742.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Simple Coherent Form <= 2.4.13 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'id' Parameter
item.description:
The Simple Coherent Form plugin (≤ 2.4.13) contains a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability (CVE-2026-14487) that allows attackers to bypass authorization checks and delete arbitrary server files. The flaw stems from insufficient path validation in `removeUploadDir`, combined with a publicly accessible nonce endpoint and a forgeable offline hash check due to a hardcoded salt. This bypass can lead to remote code execution if critical files like `wp-config.php` are removed.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f4831e75-dc0e-4d6f-b2cb-8498d8629319.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Eventer <= 4.4.2 - Insecure Password Reset Mechanism to Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Eventer plugin (≤4.4.2) contains a critical authentication bypass that allows unauthenticated attackers to reset any user’s password. The flaw occurs because the plugin stores the password reset token in plaintext within the `eventer_verification_code` user meta field, which can then be submitted to the plugin’s custom reset action to hijack accounts. This vulnerability is especially dangerous when chained with SQL injection flaws, as it enables full privilege escalation to administrator accounts.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-bc656765-1eac-4a96-99e9-c22d64984923.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WP Learn Manager <= 1.1.8 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Plugin Installation and Activation via jslearnmanager_ajax AJAX Action
item.description:
The WP Learn Manager plugin (versions ≤ 1.1.8) contains a critical authorization bypass that allows unauthenticated attackers to install and activate arbitrary plugins via the `jslearnmanager_ajax` AJAX endpoint. This flaw stems from a missing capability check on the AJAX handler, effectively granting plugin management privileges to anyone with network access to the site. Site operators must treat this as an immediate security risk until a patch is released or the plugin is removed.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-8cbf5121-2511-4e21-a346-67fa1e34fc02.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Houzez Login Register <= 3.3.3 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Houzez Login Register plugin (versions ≤ 3.3.3) contains a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to elevate their privileges to administrator. No patch has been released, making this a high-severity security issue that requires immediate action from site operators.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-19868c11-67a7-420f-911d-520e00f2f4f5.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProfileGrid – User Profiles, Groups and Communities <= 5.9.9.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Password Reset
item.description:
The ProfileGrid plugin contained a critical vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to escalate privileges by resetting arbitrary user passwords. The flaw stemmed from missing identity validation during the password update process, which permitted account takeover for any user, including administrators. This issue has been resolved in version 5.9.9.7 by enforcing strict identity verification before processing password changes.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-59aebe74-cf53-49f4-8f20-ebb5503d7dbd.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications <= 5.5.1 - Authentication Bypass to Administrator Account Takeover via 'username_b' Parameter
item.description:
The miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications plugin was patched in version 5.5.2 to resolve a critical authentication bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to hijack administrator accounts. The flaw originated in `um_reset_password_process_hook()`, which skipped server-side OTP validation and accepted an attacker-controlled `username_b` parameter to generate password-reset URLs for arbitrary users. Updating to 5.5.2 is required to restore proper session binding and role restrictions during the reset flow.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-d34f4e77-f384-4d84-be32-0d349962b614.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Membership For WooCommerce <= 3.1.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
The Membership For WooCommerce plugin contained an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability in versions up to 3.1.0. Insufficient path validation in the `[function-name]` function allowed remote attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which could be leveraged for remote code execution by targeting critical files like `wp-config.php`. The issue was resolved in version 3.1.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-0cee20a7-3730-4ee8-85db-79d9d2e9e4c4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Aimogen Pro - All-in-One AI Content Writer, Editor, ChatBot & Automation Toolkit <= 2.8.3 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
Aimogen Pro plugin versions ≤2.8.3 contained an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability caused by missing file type validation. The issue has been resolved in version 2.8.3.1, which enforces strict type and extension checks before accepting uploads. This fix prevents attackers from uploading malicious files that could lead to remote code execution.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3c601919-4026-4452-9034-b4381fe7c960.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MailOptin – Popup, Optin Forms & Email Newsletters for Mailchimp, HubSpot, AWeber Etc. <= 1.2.77.3 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The MailOptin plugin (versions ≤ 1.2.77.3) contained an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allowed attackers to elevate their user roles without credentials. The issue was resolved in version 1.2.78.0, which enforces proper capability checks to prevent unauthorized role changes.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-72633a5c-67e7-444f-9a32-ef3266468cee.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate <= 5.2.0 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
The Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate plugin contained an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in versions up to 5.2.0. The flaw allowed attackers to execute arbitrary server-side code without credentials. The vulnerability was resolved in version 5.3.0, which site administrators should apply immediately.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-7da4e3a2-29b3-47f3-b3fb-3a6ad0b8b8ac.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Super Forms <= 6.3.313 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'data' Parameter (datauristring / value)
item.description:
Super Forms 6.3.314 patches a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability present in versions up to 6.3.313. The flaw allowed attackers to bypass file type validation and capability checks on the `submit_form` AJAX handler, enabling remote code execution via two unauthenticated HTTP requests. Updating to 6.3.314 is required to close this attack vector.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-e9c7fb16-efbb-41e9-be13-98e96c1e9100.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: miniOrange Social Login and Register (Discord, Google, Twitter, LinkedIn) <= 7.7.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Administrator Account Takeover via Profile Completion OTP Flow
item.description:
The miniOrange Social Login and Register plugin (≤7.7.0) contained a critical authentication bypass in its profile completion flow that allowed unauthenticated attackers to take over administrator accounts. The vulnerability stemmed from accepting an arbitrary email address via the `email_field` POST parameter without validating it against the OAuth provider, combined with a weak OTP generation and hash leakage that enabled offline cracking. Version 7.8.0 patches this by enforcing email verification against the authenticated identity and hardening the OTP validation logic.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-a56b59ce-29c2-4172-b703-a06d7bb28da0.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core 6.9 - 7.0.1 - Remote Code Execution via REST API Batch Request Route Confusion
item.description:
A critical vulnerability in WordPress core's REST API batch endpoint (`/wp-json/batch/v1`) lets an attacker submit a sub-request that passes validation for one route but gets dispatched to a different, unintended callback. This route/validation desynchronization bypasses the `allow_batch` restriction that is supposed to limit which routes can be invoked through batching, and it also skips the target route's own argument sanitization, so attacker-controlled parameters reach internal callbacks unsanitized. Chained with a SQL injection primitive reachable through the mis-dispatched callback, the flaw allows full remote code execution on affected sites without authentication. It affects all WordPress core installs from 6.9 up to 7.0.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1ba55302-b38f-4932-bbba-cdd517380ad7.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core 6.8 - 7.0.1 - Unauthenticated SQL Injection via author__not_in Parameter
item.description:
WordPress core contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability triggered through the `author__not_in` query parameter, present in versions 6.8 through 7.0.1. The parameter was insufficiently escaped and the underlying SQL query insufficiently prepared, letting an attacker append arbitrary SQL to an existing query. Because no authentication is required to reach the vulnerable code path, any public-facing site running an affected version could have its database queried for sensitive data by an anonymous attacker. The issue is fixed in 6.8.6, 6.9.5, and 7.0.2.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-bd087d06-5395-4dfd-a288-2c3271a62842.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Easy Form Builder by WhiteStudio <= 4.0.11 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Administrator via Password Recovery REST Endpoint
item.description:
The Easy Form Builder plugin contained a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in its password recovery flow. Attackers could exploit a publicly visible session identifier (`sid`) and an unrestricted REST nonce refresh endpoint to reset any WordPress user’s password, including administrators. The vulnerability has been patched in version 4.0.12 by restricting nonce issuance and securing the password recovery token exchange.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-df8326b6-a443-4f76-a755-49f89af74d7e.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: A New Threat Landscape Meets A New Kind of Defender
item.description:
Wordfence reports the autonomous discovery of a critical WordPress Core remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability—the first of its kind in a decade—using an AI research system called PRISM. The finding underscores a shift in the threat landscape where AI-adapted prompts are rapidly identifying high-severity core flaws. Wordfence also deployed Eclipse, an AI-assisted triage pipeline, to accelerate confidential disclosure and firewall rule deployment.
Digest entry: issues/security/wordfence-blog-42539.md · Source: Wordfence Blog

item.title: Customer Support Ticket System & Helpdesk <= 6.0.5 - Unauthenticated Code Injection via 'path' Parameter
item.description:
The Customer Support Ticket System & Helpdesk plugin contained an unauthenticated code injection vulnerability in versions up to 6.0.5. Attackers could exploit the `path` parameter to invoke arbitrary PHP functions due to insufficient validation of dynamic function calls. The issue was resolved in version 6.0.6 by validating the parameter before execution, eliminating the remote code execution risk.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f9e2ad4b-716a-4a2d-87c0-2f351bd13884.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: GoDAM <= 1.12.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via WPForms File Upload Field
item.description:
The GoDAM plugin (≤1.12.2) contained a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability. The `save_video_file()` function incorrectly validated uploaded files by trusting the client-supplied `Content-Type` header instead of performing server-side MIME detection, allowing attackers to upload executable scripts directly to a web-accessible directory. Patched in version 2.0.0, this fix closes a direct path to remote code execution on affected sites.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ce3ae202-1227-4247-9133-5c7284392c9f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress <= 1.6.1 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via OAuth Authorization Endpoint
item.description:
The MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress plugin contained a critical authorization bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to escalate to administrator-equivalent access. The flaw stemmed from the plugin failing to verify user permissions on its OAuth authorization endpoint, combined with an open Dynamic Client Registration endpoint that accepted arbitrary redirect URIs. Attackers could complete the full OAuth flow without administrator interaction to obtain an admin-bound bearer token, exposing the plugin’s MCP tool surface and underlying WordPress data.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ce8ec66f-5efc-4354-8871-8e35ab4e51fc.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SAML Single Sign On <= 5.4.4 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via SAMLResponse Parameter
item.description:
The SAML Single Sign On – SSO Login plugin (≤5.4.4) contained a critical authentication bypass vulnerability. A loose boolean evaluation of `openssl_verify()` in `mo_saml_validate_signature()` incorrectly treated OpenSSL error returns (-1) as successful signature verification. This allowed unauthenticated attackers to forge SAML responses, bypass cryptographic checks, and log in as any existing WordPress user, including administrators. The issue is resolved in version 5.4.5.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b412f60f-61ea-47b1-a3ef-17275f7951df.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WP2Shell WordPress Exploit Technical Analysis and Real Attack Data
item.description:
WordPress core patched a critical vulnerability chain that allowed unauthenticated attackers to create an administrator account and subsequently execute arbitrary code. The chain combined an SQL injection in the `author__not_in` parameter (CVE-2026-60137) with a REST API batch request route confusion flaw (CVE-2026-63030). The Security Team issued forced automatic updates to close the gap across affected 6.8, 6.9, and 7.0 releases.
Digest entry: issues/security/wordfence-blog-42579.md · Source: Wordfence Blog

item.title: Demi <= 0.0.6 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Directory Deletion via demi_restore_step AJAX action
item.description:
The Demi – One Click Demo Import, Backup & Site Migration plugin contained a critical unauthenticated arbitrary directory deletion vulnerability (CVE-2026-14490) in versions up to 0.0.7. The flaw allowed attackers to recursively delete arbitrary server directories by exploiting the `demi_restore_step` AJAX endpoint, which bypassed standard WordPress capability and nonce checks when an attacker possessed an exposed HMAC signing key. The vulnerability has been patched in version 0.0.9 by restricting the AJAX handler to authenticated requests, enforcing strict path canonicalization and allow-listing, and securing the storage of signing keys and restore tokens.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-63922c28-0cb5-4abe-85ee-20b2cc6f015d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SMS Alert <= 3.9.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via 'billing_phone' Parameter
item.description:
The SMS Alert plugin (≤ 3.9.7) contained a critical authentication bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to take over any existing WordPress account by exploiting the `billing_phone` parameter during registration. The vulnerability stemmed from `processRegistration()` setting a session flag (`$_SESSION['sa_mobile_verified']`) upon OTP validation without binding it to the verified phone number, allowing an attacker to verify their own number and then swap in a victim's phone to trigger `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the victim's account. This issue has been resolved in version 3.9.8 by properly binding the verification state to the specific phone number and validating it before issuing authentication cookies.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-661d4ea9-572d-4544-b5cf-39fd69c104a6.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Advanced Responsive Video Embedder for Rumble, Odysee, YouTube, Vimeo, Kick … 10.8.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Hardcoded Backdoor in '_wplogin' Parameter
item.description:
The Advanced Responsive Video Embedder plugin (v10.8.7) contains a hardcoded backdoor that allows unauthenticated users to bypass WordPress authentication and assume any existing administrator role. The vulnerability stems from the `_arve_uc_init()` function, which runs on the `init` hook at priority 1 and validates a static SHA-256 hash against the `_wplogin` (or `_wpm`) request parameter. Because the hash is embedded directly in the plugin source, attackers can supply the known token to gain full administrative control without credentials.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-70f64ea0-5375-479f-90ac-29bcdf817cef.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Spreadsheet Price Changer for WooCommerce and WP E-commerce – Light <= 2.4.37 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Admin Account Creation
item.description:
The `user_filter` function in Spreadsheet Price Changer for WooCommerce and WP E-commerce – Light (≤ 2.4.37) lacks authorization checks, allowing unauthenticated users to create new administrator accounts. This missing authorization enables immediate privilege escalation without requiring any credentials. The plugin author has not released a patch, so the only mitigation is to remove the plugin or switch to an alternative.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1f891b68-72c4-4f94-bd49-52576ad710f9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Cost Calculator Builder PRO <= 4.0.3 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via 'orderDetails' Parameter
item.description:
The Cost Calculator Builder PRO plugin contained a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in versions up to 4.0.3. Attackers could exploit the `js_to_php` function by injecting malicious payloads into the `orderDetails[*].originalValue` field, which was passed directly to `PHP eval()` without proper sanitization. The vulnerability was patched in version 4.0.4, and all affected sites must update immediately to prevent server compromise.

item.title: Meta Box AIO <= 3.8.0 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Post Deletion via 'rwmb_frontend_field_object_id' Parameter
item.description:
Meta Box AIO versions up to 3.8.0 contain a critical missing-authorization vulnerability in the MB Frontend Submission extension that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary posts and pages. The flaw occurs because the `handle_request()` function processes the `mbfs_delete` action without verifying user capabilities or post ownership, and the nonce check is bypassed when requests arrive via `template_redirect` instead of AJAX. Site owners must update to version 3.9.0 or later to prevent unauthorized content deletion.

item.title: Admin and Site Enhancements (ASE) Pro <= 8.9.0 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via PHP Code Injection via cfgroup[input] Repeater Row Key
item.description:
The Admin and Site Enhancements (ASE) Pro plugin contained an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in versions up to 8.9.0. The flaw allowed attackers to inject arbitrary PHP code via the `cfgroup[input]` repeater row key, which was passed unsanitized into an `eval()` call inside the `recursive_html` function. The vulnerability required the `[post_cf_form]` shortcode to be present on a public page to emit the necessary nonce and session ID. Patched in version 8.9.1, this fix eliminates a critical server-side execution risk for sites using the plugin's form builder.

item.title: Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate <= 5.2.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'files[file]' Parameter via Public I/O 'set_property' Command
item.description:
The Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate (≤ 5.2.0) contains an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability that enables remote code execution. The flaw stems from a publicly registered I/O endpoint that lacks WordPress capability checks and accepts uploads via the `files[file]` parameter without validating file types. Attackers can exploit static, globally shared API credentials to bypass authentication entirely, making immediate mitigation or removal critical for affected installations.

item.title: FormGent <= 1.9.2- Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'file_token' Parameter
item.description:
The FormGent plugin contained a critical missing authorization vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files via the `file_token` parameter on the `/wp-json/formgent/responses/attachments` REST endpoint. The issue stemmed from the route being registered without authentication middleware, which also permitted path traversal bypasses on systems where the plugin’s upload directory had not yet been created. This has been resolved in version 1.10.0 by enforcing proper capability checks and validating file paths before deletion.

item.title: Single Sign On For TNG <= 2.0.0 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Unverified Password Change
item.description:
The Single Sign On For TNG plugin (≤ 2.0.0) contained a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allowed attackers to reset any user’s password, including administrators, without verification. The flaw stemmed from the `ssoprocess_ajax()` AJAX handler accepting a `setnewpassword` operation and calling WordPress’s `reset_password()` function without validating account ownership or requiring a secure token. Patched in version 2.1.0, this change closes an unverified password reset path that could lead to complete site takeover.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1d8d393e-764c-491d-8afb-7d4f8d0c387a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WooCommerce - Social Login <= 2.8.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Forged Apple 'id_token' JWT
item.description:
The WooCommerce Social Login plugin (≤2.8.7) contained a critical authentication bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user, including administrators. The vulnerability stemmed from the Apple login handler accepting a forged `id_token` JWT without verifying its cryptographic signature or validating standard claims like issuer, audience, and expiry. Because the handler resolved users solely by the email address in the decoded payload, attackers could craft a token with an admin’s email to hijack sessions. Updating to 2.8.8 is required to restore secure OAuth/JWT validation.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-53e83037-2cc5-4dc9-b55d-03829df12a65.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Membership Plugin – Kadence Memberships <= 4.0.0 - Unauthenticated Password Reset Link Poisoning to Account Takeover
item.description:
The Kadence Memberships plugin (≤4.0.0) contained a critical unauthenticated vulnerability allowing password reset link poisoning, which could lead to full account takeover. The legacy password reset handler accepted an attacker-controlled `rc_redirect` POST parameter and passed it directly to `wp_redirect()` and `add_query_arg()` without validation. When a victim clicked the poisoned reset link, the reset key was exfiltrated to the attacker, who could then replay it to hijack the account. This issue is patched in version 4.0.1.

item.title: Multi Uploader for Gravity Forms <= 1.1.8 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Media Deletion
item.description:
The Multi Uploader for Gravity Forms plugin (≤ 1.1.8) contained a critical authorization flaw allowing unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete any WordPress media attachment. The vulnerability stemmed from a missing capability check in the AJAX handler, combined with a CSRF nonce that was inadvertently exposed to the public via a JavaScript object. The issue was resolved in version 1.1.9 by enforcing proper capability verification and restricting nonce exposure.

item.title: Easy Post Submission <= 2.3.0 - Missing Authorization
item.description:

The `rbsm_submit_post` AJAX endpoint accepts a `postId` parameter and updates post metadata without verifying user capabilities. Patched in 2.4.0, this flaw enables attackers to alter titles, content, excerpts, taxonomies, and force post statuses to draft.

item.title: WordPress 7.0.4 Release
item.description:
This WordPress security release fixes an authenticated Author+ remote code execution vulnerability triggered by a malicious file upload on sites that use Imagick and Ghostscript. item.title: WordPress 7.0.3 release
item.description:
WordPress 7.0.3 is a security-only release fixing 12 separately reported vulnerabilities, headlined by a pre-authentication reflected XSS on the login screen that could be chained to PHP code execution (CVE-2026-64638 / GHSA-52p2-r8wf-jcrf). The rest are lower-privilege issues: four Contributor+ stored XSS vectors (the emoji settings element, the Post Content block, Quick Edit on large-user sites, the Post Date block), an Author+ CSS injection through a bypass of core's safe CSS attribute filter, a multisite privilege escalation letting an ordinary user create a new site where registration is open, and several information-disclosure and validation bypasses — password-protected post comments leaking through the Latest Comments block, post slug enumeration, notes disclosed in comment feeds, an email-confirmation flow bypass, and an SSRF in URL validation that permitted requests to link-local ranges. Because the login-screen bug is reachable without authentication and reportedly has a path to code execution, this is an update-now release rather than a routine minor. Fixes are being backported to every branch still eligible for security fixes (through 4.7), and 7.1 RC2 ships the applicable patches.
Digest entry: issues/security/wp-news-security-21327.md · Source: WordPress News

item.title: 40,000 WordPress Sites affected by Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in User Profile Builder WordPress Plugin

The flaw was only exploitable when the plugin's Automatically Log In setting was enabled. The issue was fixed in the latest patched release. Sites using the plugin should update immediately.

item.title: Lenxel WP <= 1.0.31 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Account Takeover
item.description:
The Lenxel WP WordPress theme is vulnerable to unauthenticated privilege escalation through account takeover in versions up to and including 1.0.31. The theme does not properly validate a user's identity before allowing updates to account details, including password changes. An unauthenticated attacker can change an arbitrary user's password, including an administrator, and then log in as that user. item.title: Webinfos <= 1.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
Webinfos for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in all versions up to and including 1.2. No known patch is available, so affected sites should remove the plugin or apply compensating controls.

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Password Reset via 'truebooker_wp_user_id'
item.description:
TrueBooker contained a missing authorization flaw in its password-reset flow. An unauthenticated attacker could supply a `truebooker_wp_user_id` value and reset the password of an arbitrary WordPress user, including administrators. This allowed account takeover without prior credentials. The issue is fixed in the patched plugin release.

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Password Reset via 'tbab-userid'
item.description:
TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 allowed unauthenticated attackers to reset arbitrary user passwords by supplying a `tbab-userid` value without proving ownership of the target account. The plugin failed to validate the user's identity before performing the password reset, enabling account takeover, including administrator accounts. Version 1.2.4 fixes the improper password reset validation.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f441477e-35b8-42ae-b71c-3fdba126021b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: AI Copilot – Content Generator <= 1.5.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Custom Workflow Route
item.description:
The AI Copilot – Content Generator plugin has an authorization bypass that allows unauthenticated visitors to create an administrator account. The issue occurs when a malicious workflow is saved and executed through the plugin's custom workflow route, using a `wp_create_user` action node with `role=administrator`. The plugin's nonce check is not a reliable authorization barrier because the `waic-nonce` value is exposed in public frontend JavaScript as `WAIC_DATA.waicNonce` when the `[aiwu-form]` shortcode or public chatbot is rendered. No patched version is listed, so affected sites should treat this as an active site-takeover risk.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-e28ae1a3-abc6-484c-abc7-1e0b958fa30b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via log Parameter
item.description:
WordPress core's login screen reflects the submitted `log` value (the username field on `wp-login.php`) back into authentication error messages without sufficient escaping, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in a victim's browser. Because the payload has to arrive with the login POST, exploitation requires tricking a visitor into submitting a crafted request — typically an auto-submitting form on an attacker-controlled page — which is why it scores 6.1 rather than higher. The fix hardens sanitization/escaping of the login error output. Notably, the vulnerable code reaches back to 4.7.0, so patched builds were shipped simultaneously for every branch from 4.7 through 7.0.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-278da117-fe04-45d6-86d4-e71fe6536032.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Emoji Settings Element
item.description:
WordPress core allowed a stored cross-site scripting payload to be smuggled into post content via the emoji settings element, because submitted post content was not sufficiently restricted. Any authenticated user at Contributor level or above could save a post carrying the payload; the script then executes when someone previews that post. Because Contributors cannot publish, the realistic trigger is an Editor or Administrator previewing a pending submission for review — meaning the script runs in a higher-privileged session. The fix shipped as a coordinated security release across every branch WordPress still backports to, from 4.7 through 7.0.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5faaf7d1-2012-42d5-affa-a5ff3388d25a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Missing Authorization to Arbitrary Site Creation on Multisite
item.description:
WordPress multisite honors a network-wide signup policy (the `registration` site option: `none`, `user`, `blog`, or `all`), but the `gimmeanotherblog` signup stage in `wp-signup.php` did not verify that policy before processing the request. On a network configured to allow user registration only (`registration` = `user`), any logged-in user at Subscriber level or above could POST the `gimmeanotherblog` stage and create a new site anyway, bypassing the network admin's intent. The fix adds the missing active-signup check to that code path. Single-site installs are not affected in any way; only multisite networks are.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-80f92f7f-72e7-4d83-9ceb-ed0e11fb8003.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Quick Edit
item.description:
WordPress core did not sufficiently escape user display names when rendering the Quick Edit (inline edit) UI on admin list tables, allowing a user who controls their own display name — Contributor role and above — to store markup that executes in the browser of any higher-privileged user who opens the affected list screen. Because a display name is persisted on the user record and re-rendered on every load of the screen, this is a stored (persistent) XSS in the wp-admin origin, not a reflected one. Wordfence notes the issue only manifests on sites with a large number of users, so the vulnerable rendering path is the alternate author-field markup core emits once a site crosses its large-user-count threshold rather than the ordinary author `<select>`. The fix is output escaping, shipped as a coordinated security release across every supported branch back to 4.7.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-92babbbf-74bd-474f-9057-c5022a7d64c7.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure via Comment Feeds
item.description:
WordPress core leaks the contents of internal notes through its public comment feeds. The comment feed output was built without excluding note-type entries, so anything written as an internal note on a post was serialized into the RSS/Atom comment feed alongside ordinary approved comments — readable by anyone, with no authentication and no interaction from a privileged user. The fix, shipped as a coordinated security release across every maintained branch, restricts comment feed output so internal notes are no longer included. Sites that never used internal notes have nothing to disclose, but the vulnerable code path is present in every listed version.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c3f9898b-0aa0-4dd1-9298-96c853dbef5c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Author+) CSS Injection
item.description:
WordPress core does not sufficiently sanitize user-supplied CSS in post content, allowing an authenticated user with Author-level capabilities or above to inject arbitrary CSS that is then rendered to other visitors on the front end. Because the injected rules are served as part of the post output, an attacker can restyle or visually rewrite pages for readers — overlaying, hiding, or replacing content that the author would not otherwise be permitted to control. The fix tightens sanitization of user-supplied CSS and has been backported across every supported (and long-tail) branch from the 4.7 line forward. This is a privilege-boundary issue, not a remote/unauthenticated one: it matters on any site where Author is not a fully trusted role.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c83a2c4d-a264-49ec-85f1-e3f48715d725.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Email Change Confirmation Bypass
item.description:
WordPress core validated a changed email address inconsistently on user-profile updates, so an authenticated user at Subscriber level or above could set a new address on their own account without completing the ownership-confirmation step core normally requires. Instead of parking the address in a pending state and waiting for the confirmation link to be followed, the affected path wrote the new address to the account directly. The fix makes validation of the submitted email consistent across the profile-update paths, so the confirmation handshake is enforced. It is a self-service bypass — the attacker changes their own account's email, not another user's — which is why it lands at CVSS 4.3 rather than in account-takeover territory.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cac1c1fa-7d6c-43c3-885e-9be320cb8f83.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Blind Server-Side Request Forgery
item.description:
Wordfence disclosed an unauthenticated blind SSRF in WordPress core affecting every release from 4.7.0 through 7.0.2. Core's outbound-request validation does not block all reserved and internal IP address ranges, so an unauthenticated attacker can induce the site to issue HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations — including hosts on the server's own private network — with the request originating from the web application rather than the attacker. The vulnerability is *blind*: the response body is not returned to the attacker, so the practical impact is enumeration of internal hosts, port/service discovery, and one-way interaction with internal endpoints that would otherwise be unreachable from the internet. Core shipped fixes across 24 maintenance branches (4.7.34 through 7.0.3).
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cddbb0f8-fc73-46d7-80af-edb69227084f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MStore API – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Cloud <= 4.20.0 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation

item.description:

item.title: QA Assistants – Driven by data <= 5.2.0.0 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:

item.title: Formidable Digital Signatures <= 3.0.6 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Signature Field
item.description:
Formidable Digital Signatures <= 3.0.6 has an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability in the plugin's `delete_file` function. Insufficient file path validation allows an attacker to delete files on the server by sending a crafted filename in `item_meta[field_id][content]` together with the `delete_saved_image` flag during a normal entry-creation POST on a form that accepts anonymous submissions. The issue is fixed in version 3.1. Sites using the plugin should upgrade immediately.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c9a5f8ca-7efc-401b-8a93-07fbe7204dce.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.3 - Authenticated (Author+) Remote Code Execution via Malicious File Upload
item.description:
WordPress core's Imagick image editor accepted uploaded files whose real content did not match their WordPress-approved extension. `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick::load()` handed the file (or stream) to Imagick without sufficient validation, so ImageMagick could identify it as a PostScript-family or compressed delegate format from magic bytes, an embedded format specifier, or decompressed content — and dispatch it to an external delegate such as Ghostscript. Because this happens automatically during attachment metadata generation, any user with `upload_files` (Author and above) could upload a crafted "image" and reach remote code execution on sites running the Imagick editor with Ghostscript available. The patched releases tighten validation in that load path so the format Imagick acts on is constrained rather than inferred from attacker-controlled content.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3f6b435b-d8b4-434b-8cac-cc3adbc437eb.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Wishlist Member X <= 3.34.1 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via 'mergewith' Parameter
item.description:
Wishlist Member versions up to 3.34.1 allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing WordPress account by passing an arbitrary user ID in the `mergewith` POST parameter during registration. The plugin's `wpm_register()` function checks the registration cookie only against the `reg` GET parameter and does not verify that `mergewith` points to a temporary or incomplete registrant tied to the current registration transaction. The attacker-controlled value is then used to update the target user's username, password, email, first name, and last name, while WordPress password and email change notifications are suppressed. If the supplied `wpm_id` does not match a membership level, the update payload omits the role key, so `wp_update_user()` preserves the target's existing role, including administrator.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-84afe5a7-1bf4-4b83-bf77-efbb003a30cd.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: RapiSafe <= 1.0.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'rsmfcf7_session' and 'file_name' Parameters
item.description:
RapiSafe's upload-removal AJAX handler allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files because it trusts client-supplied session and file-name values without adequate path validation. The handler's nonce is exposed in public JavaScript, so an attacker can obtain it from any Contact Form 7 page that renders a RapiSafe upload field. No patch is available, so the practical response is to remove or disable the plugin.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-49f67bbb-cbd0-40ae-ae00-9cb72b041e22.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: 6Storage Rentals <= 2.27.0 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via 'email' Parameter
item.description:
The 6Storage Rentals plugin exposes an unauthenticated account takeover flaw in the `six_storage_create_wp_user()` AJAX handler. The handler is reachable without authentication and can establish a session for any WordPress user whose email address is supplied. This allows an attacker to log in as an existing account, including an administrator, without credentials.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-94e987be-bdfc-4691-b250-2b7d7249df0a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: User Session Synchronizer <= 1.4.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via 'ussync-key', 'ussync-token', and 'ussync-ref' Parameters
item.description:
User Session Synchronizer's session synchronization handler can be abused by an unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators. The handler trusts attacker-controlled `ussync-key`, `ussync-token`, and `ussync-ref` request parameters without nonce, capability, or shared-secret validation. When an unregistered `ussync-key` is supplied, fallback behavior makes the encryption key and referer check predictable, allowing a crafted `ussync-ref` value to trigger `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for a matched user. No patch is reported, so affected installations should be treated as potentially compromised.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cbc32e6d-47c5-4050-ba77-5a54203fe56a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: User Profile Builder <= 3.16.4 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Type Confusion to Administrator Account Takeover via 'username' Parameter
item.description:
User Profile Builder's registration flow calls `absint()` on the return value of `wp_insert_user()` *before* testing it with `is_wp_error()`. When core rejects a registration — specifically for a username of 61–70 characters — it returns a `WP_Error` object, but `absint()` has already coerced that object to the integer `1`, so the `is_wp_error()` guard never fires and execution continues as if user ID 1 had just been created. The plugin then issues its transient-backed autologin nonce bound to user ID 1, letting an unauthenticated visitor log in as the site's administrator. Fixed in 3.16.5; anything up to and including 3.16.4 is exploitable with a single crafted registration submission and no authentication.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-9f606fba-f779-42ea-a160-6c3b20dc5e79.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.6 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Insecure Direct Object Reference in 'truebooker_wp_user_id' Parameter
item.description:
TrueBooker's `add_front_user_update()` AJAX handler is exposed to unauthenticated requests and trusts a caller-supplied `truebooker_wp_user_id` parameter, passing it straight to `wp_update_user()` with no authentication or ownership check. Any anonymous visitor can therefore rewrite the email address on any account on the site, including an administrator's. Once the email is changed, the attacker triggers WordPress's own lost-password flow and receives the reset link at their own inbox, completing a full administrator takeover. Fixed in 1.2.7; everything up to and including 1.2.6 is exploitable.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f0d3f7cb-4974-4b0f-9658-1895e5966276.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Link Library <= 7.9.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via link_url Parameter
item.description:
Link Library's link-deletion routine accepted an unvalidated file path from the `link_url` parameter, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion when the optional local-file deletion setting was enabled and an administrator permanently deleted a submitted link. The vulnerability can lead to remote code execution if a critical file such as `wp-config.php` is deleted. The patched release corrects the path validation in the deletion flow.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-41327dfa-db64-476a-a263-7bd4f69fb857.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Solace Extra <= 1.6.0 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Site Content Deletion and Unauthorized Demo Import via action-import-zip AJAX Action
item.description:
Solace Extra has a missing capability check on the `import_zip()` AJAX handler, allowing low-privilege users to delete site content and trigger demo imports. The handler is registered for both authenticated and unauthenticated AJAX requests and relies only on an `ajax-nonce` nonce that is exposed on admin pages. This can wipe navigation menus, sidebar widgets, theme mods, and Elementor templates. The patched release addresses the missing authorization.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4e427c4e-3e27-49e3-ba64-6241b430d5d8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Pods <= 3.3.9 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Authorization Bypass to Admin Methods via 'pods_admin' AJAX Router
item.description:
The Pods plugin had an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in its `pods_admin` AJAX router. Access checks were funneled through `pods_error()`, which under the JSON meta-box-loader compatibility path only wrote failures to the PHP error log and returned `false` instead of terminating the request. As a result, the method allowlist, nonce verification, login enforcement, and capability gate did not block requests, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to reach admin methods, escalate to Administrator, or overwrite any user's password. The fix restores request termination when authorization checks fail.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3628032a-3121-45a7-8a78-cfcd8ba6af2f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Frontend Admin by DynamiApps <= 3.29.9 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'item_id' Parameter
item.description:
The plugin's user-update AJAX flow could be abused to bypass a capability check and take over the default administrator account. The bypass occurred when a non-numeric `item_id` value caused the `edit_user` check to be skipped, allowing a signed ACF objects payload to be processed with a user ID that WordPress coerced to `1`. The fix closes the authorization gap in the user update path.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-01404fad-7b5a-485a-b557-c608fe25e6c9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProSolution WP Client <= 2.0.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'newfilename' and 'filename' Parameters
item.description:
ProSolution WP Client is vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion caused by insufficient path validation in `proSol_fileDeleteProcess`. An attacker can first call `proSol_fileUploadModalProcess` to poison their session with a path-traversal key, then call `proSol_fileDeleteProcess` using that key as the `filename` parameter. Both steps require only the publicly exposed frontend nonce. Deleting files such as `wp-config.php` can lead to remote code execution.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4e9698f0-b228-4f4e-838b-c0c0a193d675.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProSolution WP Client <= 2.0.10 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Content-Disposition Header Filename Override
item.description:
The ProSolution WP Client plugin has an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in `proSol_handleFileUpload` that can lead to remote code execution. The handler trusts an attacker-controlled `Content-Disposition` header filename, which overrides the allow-listed multipart filename before the file is saved, and a post-save extension check does not delete the already-written file. The nonce required to reach the upload handler is publicly exposed via `wp_localize_script` on front-end pages rendering the job portal shortcode, allowing unauthenticated visitors to bypass that gating check. Sites should update to the patched release immediately.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3c4a7aef-09ec-4d17-87d6-f507d64e0afa.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence
